title: Premature Batching of Simple DB Writes
pattern: Queueing and batching single, low-frequency database updates or inserts to "save transaction overhead."
why_bad: Batching adds massive thread synchronization complexity, queue maintenance, and dramatically increases the average response latency of user-facing transactions. If database transaction rates are low, individual synchronous writes are extremely fast and keep the code simple [142].
detection: The presence of timers, buffers, or queues to delay simple database updates until a threshold size is met in low-traffic or single-user systems.
counterexample: High-throughput systems (like analytics logs processors receiving > 10,000 requests per second) where batching is mandatory. `Contextual`.
fix: Write updates synchronously to the database immediately when they occur.
